title: P.E.R.C. NO. 2026-45
text:
P.E.R.C. NO. 2026-45
STATE OF NEW JERSEY
BEFORE THE PUBLIC EMPLOYMENT RELATIONS COMMISSION
In the Matter of
SOUTH ORANGE-MAPLEWOOD BOARD
OF EDUCATION,
Petitioner,
-and- Docket No. SN-2026-019
SOUTH ORANGE-MAPLEWOOD EDUCATION
ASSOCIATION,
Respondent.
SYNOPSIS
The Public Employment Relations Commission grants the
Board's request for a restraint of binding arbitration of the
Association's grievance, alleging that the Board violated the
parties' CNA by assigning non-negotiated duties to teachers
outside of scheduled lunch periods. To the extent the
Association contests the assignment of these duties, the
Commission finds that the grievance is not legally arbitrable
because the assignment of these duties is related to student
safety and supervision. The Commission further finds that
Association has not established that the Board’s assigned
supervisory duties have adversely impacted the teachers’
compensation, workload, or preparation time, and thus, this
record does not establish severable impact issues that could be
arbitrable.
This synopsis is not part of the Commission decision. It
has been prepared for the convenience of the reader. It has been
neither reviewed nor approved by the Commission.

P.E.R.C. NO. 2026-45
STATE OF NEW JERSEY
BEFORE THE PUBLIC EMPLOYMENT RELATIONS COMMISSION
In the Matter of
SOUTH ORANGE-MAPLEWOOD BOARD
OF EDUCATION,
Petitioner,
-and- Docket No. SN-2026-019
SOUTH ORANGE-MAPLEWOOD EDUCATION
ASSOCIATION,
Respondent.
Appearances:
For the Petitioner, Lenox, Socey, Formidoni, Giordano,
Carrigg, Lang & Casey, LLC, attorneys (Patrick F.
Carrigg, of counsel; Victoria R. Lang, on the brief)
For the Respondent, Selikoff & Cohen, P.A., attorneys
(Keith Waldman, of counsel and on the brief; Liz Pudel,
on the brief)
DECISION
On November 19, 2025, the South Orange-Maplewood Board of
Education (Board) filed a scope of negotiations petition seeking
a restraint of binding arbitration of a grievance filed by the
South Orange-Maplewood Education Association (Association). The
grievance asserts that the Board violated Article XXI(7)(g) of
the parties’ collective negotiations agreement (CNA) by assigning
non-negotiated duties (corridor duty, office support duty, and
content lab area duty) to teachers outside of scheduled lunch
periods.
The Board filed briefs, exhibits, and the certification of

P.E.R.C. NO. 2026-45 2.
its Superintendent. The Association filed a brief and the
certification of its Chairperson for the Professional Rights and
Responsibilities Committee (Association Chairperson). These
facts appear.
The Association represents certified teaching employees and
non-certified supportive employees. The Board and Association
were parties to a CNA with a term from July 1, 2021 through June
30, 2024, which continues in effect. The grievance procedure
ends in binding arbitration.
Article XXI(7)(g) of the parties’ CNA, entitled “Employee
Hours and Employee Work Load,” provides in pertinent part:
All middle school teachers shall be assigned
to one daily - related duty period, which may
include cafeteria and/or corridor. The duty
assignment shall be rotated among all middle
school teachers so that a teacher will not be
required to perform more than one duty per
school week. Rotation is intended to be no
more than once every five school days
distributed on an equitable basis.
The Superintendent certifies that the Association initiated
a “Level I” oral grievance concerning a teacher’s assignment to
non-instructional duties of corridor duty, office supervision
duty, and content area lab duty. That grievance was denied.
On September 7, 2025, the Association elevated the grievance
to Level II. On September 16, the Level II grievance was denied,
as follows:
Our assigned duties support safe supervision
of students and allow us to carry out Board

P.E.R.C. NO. 2026-45 3.
Policy 3280 excerpted below.
1. Each teaching staff member shall
maintain a standard of care for member’s
assigned duties and responsibilities.
2. A teaching staff member shall not
voluntarily assume responsibility for duties
he or she cannot reasonably perform. Such
assumed responsibilities carry the same
potential for liability as do assigned
responsibilities.
All assigned staff duties for the 2025-2026
school year support the safety of students.
[Exhibit D, Board. Cert. Emphasis added.]
The grievance was then elevated to Level III. On October 1,
2025, the Superintendent denied the grievance, citing Commission
precedent and stating in pertinent part:
Consistent with these precedents, the
District’s assignment of corridor duty,
office supervision duty, and content area lab
duty is a substitution of one student-
supervision location for another within the
middle school. These duties are student
supervisory in nature and directly tied to
the District’s responsibility to ensure
student safety, security, and appropriate
conduct.
Therefore, as the grievance seeks to prevent
District administration from exercising its
managerial prerogative to assign duties
necessary for student supervision and safety,
the grievance is respectfully denied.
[Exhibit E, Board Cert. Emphasis added.]
On October 3, 2025, the Association filed a “Level IV”

P.E.R.C. NO. 2026-45 4.
grievance,1/ stating in pertinent part:
[The Board] has directed teachers to perform
duties that are not in the [CNA]. These
duties include corridor duty, office support
duty, and content area lab duty and they are
scheduled to occur outside of the scheduled
lunch periods. They do not comply with the
defined lunch-related duties in the contract.
* * *
Remedies Sought:
1. [The Board] cease and desist immediately
the practice of assigning non-negotiated
duties.
2. [The Board] provide compensation at the
class coverage rate for the members who have
performed these duties....
[Exhibit F, Board Cert.]
On October 30, 2025, the Board held a public board meeting
in which it, by resolution, denied the Level IV grievance in part
and affirmed it in part, stating in pertinent part:
WHEREAS, it has been determined that the
assigned duties constitute reasonable and
necessary supervisory responsibilities
inherent to the role of teaching staff
members and do not violate the specific
provisions cited, as they are not deemed
“lunch-related duties” that infringe upon the
contractually defined duty-free lunch period;
* * *
Maplewood Middle School will cease the
assignment of the office support duty. The
other duty assignments are student
1/ This is the first written statement in the instant record
articulating the Association’s grievance.

P.E.R.C. NO. 2026-45 5.
supervisory duties that are not subject to
negotiations and may be assigned by the
administration.
The Association Chairperson’s 8-paragraph certification
contains one paragraph addressing the grievance at issue.2/ That
paragraph states only that the Association’s grievance is
“challenging the unilateral imposition of non-instructional
duties on teaching staff members, including but not limited to
office supervision duty.”3/
On November 12, 2025, the Association filed a Request for
Submission of a Panel of Arbitrators, which identifies the
grievance to be arbitrated as, “Principal directed teachers to
perform duties outside the time defined in the collective
bargaining agreement.” This petition ensued.
Our jurisdiction is narrow. The Commission is addressing
the abstract issue of whether the subject matter in dispute is
within the scope of collective negotiations. We do not consider
the merits of the grievance or any contractual defenses that the
employer may have. Ridgefield Park Ed. Ass’n v. Ridgefield Park
Bd. of Ed., 78 N.J. 144, 154 (1978).
2/ The remainder of the certification pertains to other
Association grievances.
3/ As noted above, the Board’s October 30 resolution
discontinued the assignment of “office support duty,”
thereby granting that aspect of the Association’s grievance,
but stated that the remaining assignments are student
supervisory duties.

P.E.R.C. NO. 2026-45 6.
The Supreme Court of New Jersey articulated the standards
for determining whether a subject is mandatorily negotiable in
Local 195, IFPTE v. State, 88 N.J. 393, 404-405 (1982):
[A] subject is negotiable between public
employers and employees when (1) the item
intimately and directly affects the work and
welfare of public employees; (2) the subject
has not been fully or partially preempted by
statute or regulation; and (3) a negotiated
agreement would not significantly interfere
with the determination of governmental
policy. To decide whether a negotiated
agreement would significantly interfere with
the determination of governmental policy, it
is necessary to balance the interests of the
public employees and the public employer.
When the dominant concern is the government’s
managerial prerogative to determine policy, a
subject may not be included in collective
negotiations even though it may intimately
affect employees’ working conditions.
We must balance the parties’ interests in light of the
particular facts and arguments presented. City of Jersey City v.
Jersey City POBA, 154 N.J. 555, 574-575 (1998).
The Board argues that the Association’s grievance is not
arbitrable because it significantly interferes with its
managerial prerogative to assign teaching staff duties related to
student safety and supervision. The Board asserts these duties -
corridor and content-area lab duty - are not clerical, custodial,
or tangential, but are connected to the Board’s obligation to
protect students and safely operate the school. The Board argues
that “corridor duty” ensures safe student movement between
classes and “lab duty” requires oversight of students in

P.E.R.C. NO. 2026-45 7.
environments involving specialized equipment with heightened
safety considerations. The Board further argues that the
assigned safety duties do not substitute a preparation period for
supervisory duty, but rather, are simply substituting one form of
student supervision (e.g., lunch duty) for another within the
school day.
The Association argues that the grievance is arbitrable
because it is challenging the manner in which these non-
instructional duties are distributed amongst the teachers and the
resulting impacts on the teachers’ compensation, workload, and
preparatory time. The Association asserts these issues are
severable from the non-negotiable assignment of the student
supervision for safety purposes. The Association contends that
the severable and negotiable impacts of the supervision duties
are issues of fact for an arbitrator to determine. The
Association asserts that the method of distributing safety
supervision assignments and compensation for performing them are
mandatorily negotiable and arbitrable, particularly if such
assignments increase workload or reduce preparatory time.
The assignment of non-teaching duties related to student
safety, control, or supervision are not mandatorily negotiable.
Byram Tp. Bd. of Ed., P.E.R.C. No. 76-27 (1976), aff’d 152 N.J.
Super. 12 (App. Div. 1977). Moreover, employers are not required
to negotiate over “minor tasks incidental to [a public

P.E.R.C. NO. 2026-45 8.
employee’s] primary duties.” Bayonne Bd. of Ed. P.E.R.C. No. 87-
109, 13 NJPER 268 (¶18110 1987); see also New Jersey Highway
Auth. v. IFPTE Local 193 (Toll Supervisors of Am.), AFL-CIO, 2003
N.J. Super. Unpub. LEXIS 20 (App. Div. 2003). However, the
method of distributing these assignments, compensation for
performing them, as well as reductions in preparation time and
increases in workload are mandatorily negotiable and arbitrable
issues. Long Branch Bd. of Ed., P.E.R.C. No. 93-8, 18 NJPER 403
(¶23182 1992).
The documented responses of the Board throughout the
grievance process consistently reflect that the assignment of
non-teaching duties in the instant dispute is related to safety
and student supervision. Thus, based on the above cited
precedent, to the extent the Association contests the assignment
of these duties, the grievance is not legally arbitrable.
The Association’s Level IV grievance also seeks compensation
for performing these non-teaching duties. However, the Board’s
response to the Level III grievance, and the Superintendent’s
certification, provide that these supervisory duties do not
increase the teacher’s student supervision time and are “a
substitution of one student-supervision location [e.g. lunch
duty] for another within the middle school.” In contrast, the
Association’s certification contains no support that the
teachers’ workload or compensation has been impacted by these

P.E.R.C. NO. 2026-45 9.
supervisory assignments.4/ Compare Ocean Cty. Vocational
Technical Sch. P.E.R.C. No. 2019-29, 45 NJPER 301 (¶78
2019)(denying a restraint of arbitration of a grievance
challenging a secretary’s assignment of breakfast duties without
additional compensation, where she certified that her
compensation and workload were impacted.); see also Tp. of
Lyndhurst, P.E.R.C. No. 2017-41, 43 NJPER 301 (¶85
2017)(restraining arbitration of a grievance challenging a
Township ordinance restricting off-duty police work because the
Association did not produce any evidence of claimed severable
impact issues.); Clark Tp., P.E.R.C. No. 2016-55, 42 NJPER 372
(¶105 2016), aff’d, No. A-2544-15T3, 2016 N.J. Super. Unpub.
LEXIS 2348 (App. Div. Oct. 28, 2016)(restraining arbitration
regarding alleged severable impact issues because the union did
not produce any evidence demonstrating that the grievant’s
workload increased as a result of the Township’s unilateral
change to her work hours/schedule.)
We acknowledge Commission precedent cited by the Association
supporting that a grievance may develop as it proceeds through
the grievance process.5/ However, that precedent is not
4/ We also note that the Association provided no support for a
severable compensation claim for the office duty that was
discontinued by the Board.
5/ The Commission determines scope of negotiations petitions
based on the totality of the certified facts and arguments
(continued...)

P.E.R.C. NO. 2026-45 10.
applicable to the instant matter where the Association has not
certified to severable impacts from the disputed assignments. In
the absence of certified facts from the Association that the
Board’s assigned supervisory duties have adversely impacted the
teachers’ compensation, workload, or preparation time, this
record is insufficient to establish severable impact issues.
For the foregoing reasons, we grant the Board’s request for
a restraint of binding arbitration of the Association’s
grievance.
ORDER
South Orange-Maplewood Board of Education’s request for a
restraint of binding arbitration is granted.
BY ORDER OF THE COMMISSION
Chair Hennessy-Shotter, Commissioners Eaton, Davey, Hines, and
Papero voted in favor of this decision. None opposed.
Commissioner Higgins was not present.
ISSUED: June 25, 2026
Trenton, New Jersey

raised by the parties and has often acknowledged that a
dispute becomes more sharply focused as the grievance
proceeds and professional assistance is received at higher
levels of the grievance process. See North Hunterdon Reg.
